novel_features.name: Net balance overview
novel_features.description: See everything you owe and are owed across every friend and group in one net-position view.
novel_features.rationale: Splitwise returns balances separately per group and per friend; no client aggregates them into a single net position.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of separate get-groups + get-friends calls when an agent needs the user's overall money position.

novel_features.name: Settle-up plan
novel_features.description: Compute the minimum set of transfers that zeroes out balances in a group, then optionally record the payments (print-only by default; --record writes real payment expenses to your Splitwise account).
novel_features.rationale: Requires a min-cash-flow debt-simplification graph over per-member net balances; no Splitwise client emits a transfer plan.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a group wants the fewest transfers to get everyone to zero, previewed before anything is recorded.

novel_features.name: Audit before settling
novel_features.description: Catch duplicate settlement rows and abnormal expense amounts before you trust a settle-up plan.
novel_features.rationale: Requires scanning the full synced history for duplicate payment:true rows and computing median/MAD cost outliers per category; no endpoint flags either.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this before settle-up or report so a duplicate settlement or an outlier expense doesn't get baked into a transfer plan.

novel_features.name: Debt aging
novel_features.description: List who owes you (and whom you owe) sorted by how long the balance has gone unsettled.
novel_features.rationale: Requires computing days since each friend's last-settled point from synced expenses and payment:true settlements; no single API call returns aging.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the task is 'who never pays me back' or chasing stale IOUs, not just the current balance.

novel_features.name: Spend analytics rollups
novel_features.description: Total shared spend broken down by category, group, or month from your synced history.
novel_features.rationale: Requires summing synced expense amounts bucketed locally; Splitwise has no analytics, no spend-over-time, no per-category rollups.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for any 'how much did we spend on X' question instead of paging the whole expense list.

novel_features.name: Fairness lenses
novel_features.description: See who's carrying more than their share of cost, and how likely a stale balance is to actually get paid.
novel_features.rationale: Requires classifying members as carrier vs rider from local paid/owed shares and projecting a settle date from settlement episode history; no endpoint offers either lens.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the question is who's owed the most relative to what they've paid, not just the raw balance.

novel_features.name: Cross-group netting
novel_features.description: Collapse a person's balance across every group and non-group expense into the minimum set of real-world transfers.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a debt graph over every synced group and friend balance with cycle-cancelling min-transfer math; Splitwise's simplify-debts is scoped to one group at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when one person's balance is scattered across multiple groups and one-off expenses and you want the fewest real transfers, not a per-group snapshot.

novel_features.name: Trip/period report
novel_features.description: Turn synced trip or period spend into a shareable summary plus per-person and per-category export.
novel_features.rationale: Requires assembling multiple local rollups into one document; Splitwise's own export is a per-group CSV with none of these sections.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for an end-of-trip or end-of-month writeup, or as a generic JSON/CSV sink into an external workflow tool.

novel_features.name: Group ledger with running balance
novel_features.description: Every expense in a group, in date order, with a cumulative running balance per member.
novel_features.rationale: Requires replaying synced expenses in order against per-member shares; the API only returns current balances, never the running history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to audit how a group's balances got to where they are, not just the snapshot. Add --friend to replay one person across every group instead of one group's members.

novel_features.name: Split calculator
novel_features.description: Build and preview the exact expense split (equal, exact, percentage, or shares) before recording it.
novel_features.rationale: create_expense requires a per-user paid_share/owed_share array that sums exactly to the total; no Splitwise client computes and previews that body for you.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to turn 'I paid $84, split equally with the trip' into a ready-to-record expense without hand-building the share arrays. Add --record to submit it.

novel_features.name: Recurring-expense detector
novel_features.description: Surface repeating charges (rent, utilities, subscriptions) from your synced history and flag a cycle missing an expected entry.
novel_features.rationale: Requires grouping synced expenses by normalized description and cadence in SQLite with a regularity gate; Splitwise has no recurrence concept and no endpoint that returns it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to catch a shared monthly bill nobody remembered to log this cycle.

novel_features.name: Fairness nudge
novel_features.description: Post a payment reminder as a comment on the actual open expense thread, previewed before it sends (print-only by default; --send posts a real comment your friend will see).
novel_features.rationale: Requires resolving a friend to their specific open expense locally and posting through create_comment; no client turns a stale balance into a targeted reminder.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to nudge one person about a specific unpaid expense instead of a generic message outside Splitwise.

novel_features.name: Balances by group
novel_features.description: See one row per group per currency for every non-zero balance, without the noise of settled groups.
novel_features.rationale: Requires filtering and reshaping the same local join that powers balances into a per-group-per-currency view; no endpoint returns this grouping directly.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the question is scoped to 'which groups do I still owe in', not the single net number.

novel_features.name: Agent brief
novel_features.description: Get one compact digest of net position, the stalest debts, and what changed since last sync in a single call.
novel_features.rationale: Composes three local reads (balances, debts --aged, activity) into one bounded payload sized for the canonical MCP output-bounding contract; no single endpoint or client returns a state digest.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this first at the start of a session instead of three separate calls; use balances, debts --aged, or activity directly when you need the full detail behind one of these numbers.

novel_features.name: Store reconcile
novel_features.description: Verify the local store actually matches Splitwise before you trust a settle-up or report (calls the live Splitwise API; needs SPLITWISE_API_KEY and network).
novel_features.rationale: Requires paging live get_expenses with updated_after and diffing IDs/updated_at/deleted_at against the local store; a prior sync bug silently dropped 43 of 143 expenses with no other way to detect it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this before a settle-up or report when a number looks wrong, or as a routine pre-settle check.

novel_features.name: Activity diff
novel_features.description: Show what changed since your last sync — new, edited, and deleted expenses to review.
novel_features.rationale: Requires diffing synced notifications and updated_after expenses against the local store's last-sync cursor.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to reconcile recent account activity before settling or reporting.

novel_features.name: Forecast
novel_features.description: See what shared bills are expected next, projected from your recurring-expense history.
novel_features.rationale: Requires projecting forward from the recurring cadence model over local SQLite; Splitwise has no forecasting or upcoming-bill concept.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for 'what's coming up' instead of recurring, which only detects the pattern of bills already logged.

novel_features.name: Normalize
novel_features.description: Express multi-currency spend in one base currency, using rates you supply, with anything unconverted called out honestly.
novel_features.rationale: Requires converting locally-synced spend totals with user-supplied rates and explicitly listing what could not be converted; Splitwise never converts currencies across groups for you.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when spend spans more than one currency and you want one honest number, not a silently-dropped or auto-converted total.

narrative.headline: Every Splitwise feature, plus an offline SQLite ledger that powers balance, debt-aging, spend analytics, fairness, and full-text search no other Splitwise tool has.
narrative.value_prop: splitwise-pp-cli wraps the full Splitwise API — expenses, groups, friends, comments, settle-ups — and keeps a local copy of your whole ledger. That local store powers a net `balances` view, `debts --aged` (who never pays you back), `spend` rollups by category or month, offline `search`, a group `ledger` with running balances, `fairness` and `net` for who's carrying cost and how balances collapse across groups, and a `settle-up` plan that minimizes transfers. `brief` gives an agent one bounded state digest, and `reconcile` verifies the local store still matches Splitwise before you trust any of it. Fuzzy name resolution means you never paste a numeric ID.
narrative.auth_narrative: Splitwise authenticates with a personal API key used as an HTTP Bearer token. Register an app at https://secure.splitwise.com/apps to get your key, then set SPLITWISE_API_KEY. The Splitwise API also offers OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code) for multi-user apps, but this CLI authenticates as a single user with a personal API key only — there is no OAuth login flow in the binary.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary, config path, and verify state without needing credentials.
Pull the last 30 days of groups, friends, and expenses into the local store.
See your net position across every friend and group at a glance.
Get one compact digest — net position, stalest debts, and recent changes — in a single call.

troubleshoots.fix: Set SPLITWISE_API_KEY to a key from https://secure.splitwise.com/apps, then run splitwise-pp-cli doctor.
Run splitwise-pp-cli sync first — these read the local store, which is empty until synced.
Splitwise has conservative personal-use limits; re-run sync later, or use sync --since 7d for incremental pulls.
Run splitwise-pp-cli reconcile to see what's missing against the live API, then splitwise-pp-cli sync --full to force a complete re-pull.

troubleshoots.symptom: `get-expenses --data-source local` (or the offline fallback) returns only 20 rows even with `--all`
troubleshoots.fix: Pass an explicit `--limit`, e.g. `splitwise-pp-cli get-expenses --data-source local --limit 5000 --json`; this build applies the default page size to local reads and `--all` does not lift it. The hand-built commands (ledger, spend, report, audit, …) read the whole local mirror and are unaffected.

troubleshoots.symptom: `net`, `balances --by-group`, `report` show `you_id: 0` / `Your net: 0.00`, or `split --equal` says `--paid-by is required when current user is not synced`
troubleshoots.fix: Run `splitwise-pp-cli sync --resources get-current-user` once; the default `sync` covers the list resources but not the single current-user object.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for splitwise-pp-cli when a task involves shared expenses, group trips, roommate bills, or settling up — logging an expense, checking who owes whom, aging a stale debt, rolling up spend by category, finding a past expense, checking who's carrying more than their share, or computing a settle-up plan. It is the right tool when you want offline analytics or a verified local copy of a Splitwise account, not a one-off live lookup. Under --agent every command wraps its payload as {"meta": {...}, "results": ...}; --json returns the bare payload. When a task needs an id for a friend, group, or category name, call resolve first; every id-taking command (ledger, settle-up, get-friend, get-group) accepts the id it returns.
anti_triggers: do not use for live FX conversion — normalize takes user-supplied rates
do not use to pay anyone — it records settlements in Splitwise only
do not use for multi-user OAuth apps — the CLI authenticates as a single user with a personal API key
do not use for real-time push notifications — sync and reconcile are both pull-based, not a live feed

recipes.title: Net position for an agent
recipes.explanation: Returns just the headline numbers an agent needs to report the user's overall money position.

recipes.title: Inspect a group's members and balances (narrow a verbose payload)
recipes.explanation: get-groups returns deeply nested members and balance arrays; --select with dotted paths keeps only the fields you need so an agent doesn't burn context on the full payload.

recipes.title: Verify the local store before trusting it
recipes.explanation: Diffs the local store against live get_expenses and reports anything missing, stale, or deleted remotely before you build a settle-up or report on it.

recipes.title: One-shot agent state check
recipes.explanation: Returns net position, the stalest debts, and recent activity in one bounded call instead of three separate fan-out calls.

recipes.title: Plan the fewest transfers to settle a trip
recipes.explanation: Prints the minimum-transfer settle-up plan; add --record to create the payment expenses.

recipes.title: Who is carrying the cost in a group
recipes.explanation: Classifies each member as carrier or rider from paid vs owed shares; --by risk and --by collectability switch lenses. The --agent output is wrapped as {meta, results}.

recipes.title: Turn a friend, group, or category name into its id
recipes.explanation: Use resolve whenever you need an id for a name: it matches the local store (no network) and returns the candidate records. Do not page through get-friends or get-groups and grep for a name; resolve is the id lookup.
